text: Hello and welcome to live coverage of the Premier League clash between Fulham and Manchester United at Craven Cottage.

It has been a solid week for the Cottagers, picking up a decent point on the road at Brighton last weekend in the Premier League before easing past Championship side Ipswich Town on Wednesday to reach the EFL Cup quarter-finals for the first time since the 2004-05 campaign.
All in all, it has been a reasonable start to Fulham's second season back in the top-flight, currently 14th and seven points above the bottom three.

In contrast to their hosts, United's week has been a tough one, suffering back-to-back 3-0 defeats at Old Trafford, firstly against rivals Manchester City in the Premier League and then Newcastle United to crash out of the EFL Cup.

Erik ten Hag is a man under pressure, though his team have been better on the road this season, picking up nine points from a possible 15, and that away form could give the Red Devils a much-needed confidence boost heading into this one.
Marco Silva rung the changes for the cup win at Portman Road in midweek, and a lot of his key players return as Leno replaces Rodak between the sticks while Ream and Robinson come into the back four.
Iwobi and Willian are preferred to De Cordova-Reid and Cairney, while star midfielder Palhinha will hold in midfield.
The big news for United is that Marcus Rashford is absent from the squad altogether.

The official line is he has failed a fitness test, though Rashford has been criticised by some for celebrating his birthday hours after the derby defeat last weekend, including his own boss, who described his actions as "unacceptable".

Ten Hag makes six changes from the Newcastle defeat, with Hojlund and Fernandes in for Martial and Hannibal in attack while McTominay and Eriksen come into the midfield, replacing the benched Mount and the injured Casemiro, who will be out for several weeks.
Wan-Bissaka made his return against the Magpies and will start at right-back, while Evans replaces Lindelof.
Varane remains on the bench.
The two teams enter the pitch at Craven Cottage, and kick-off is now just moments away!
The visitors kick us off, and we are underway!
United may have a problem here very early on as Maguire puts the ball out under seemingly no pressure before dropping to his haunches.
Just moments before going down, Maguire and Rodrigo clashed and the United man's head seemed to come off the forward's shoulder.
He looks a little dazed.
Maguire is going to try and soldier on having received some treatment.
That is one to keep an eye on, for sure.
It will be interesting to see how United cope without Rashford, though they have done well without him previously.

Since the start of 2021-22, in the Premier League United have a higher win percentage (10/16 - 62.5 per cent) and points per game (2.1) without Rashford than with him (34/70 - 48.6 per cent) and 1.6 ppg.
Palhinha perhaps a little fortunate not to receive a yellow card for bringing down Fernandes with a sliding challenge.
The visitors will have a free-kick in a great crossing position.
GOAL!!! MCTOMINAY PUTS UNITED AHEAD!!! Eriksen floats the free-kick towards the back post, where Garnacho is waiting to divert the ball back across the face of goal.

McTominay is on his toes in the middle and pokes home to put the visitors 1-0 up! That is the start they needed, though there is a VAR check to ascertain whether there was an offside in the build-up...
This is a very lengthy check, and Maguire is the player in question despite not touching the ball.
He is offside and appears to go for the ball, so it will be interesting to see what the verdict is...
NO GOAL!!! Maguire is deemed to be offside and impacting the play, and McTominay's goal is wiped out! That is a big let-off for Fulham.
How will United respond?
Since winning back-to-back Premier League games against United in March/December 2009, Fulham are now winless in their last 15 against them (three draws, 12 defeats).
Fulham break and Willian shows some neat footwork to make the space for a shot, though Wan-Bissaka makes an important block before Wilson is caught offside.
Antony sloppily loses the ball and Fulham look to catch United out on the counter, with plenty of white shirts flying forward.
However, Robinson's cross towards the back post is dealt with by Dalot, who nods the ball away from danger.
There are some tame appeals for a penalty as Fernandes goes down under Bassey's challenge, though the protests were half-hearted at best and the referee waves play on.
Palhinha catches the United defence out with a quick free-kick, setting Willian away down the left.
The winger takes the ball right into the heart of the United penalty area, but Wan-Bissaka does well to get back into position and block the shot.
United are yet to have a shot in this game, and the likes of Fernandes and Hojlund have just not been a factor to this point.
They will need to get their key attacking players more involved.

United have won their last six Premier League away games against Fulham – only at West Bromwich Albion (eight between 1984 and 2011) have they won more consecutively at an opponent in their league history.

Willian arrows a cross towards the back post where it looks for all the world like Wilson will fire home, until Dalot bails out his team with a superb defensive intervention, intercepting at the vital moment.
Robinson wipes out Antony with a poor challenge and picks up the first yellow card of the game.
A Fernandes corner from the left is cleared, but only to Evans.
He goes for the acrobatic volley, but looks every bit the centre-back as he lashes high over the crossbar.
The ball sits up nicely for Fernandes to hit from just outside the Fulham penalty area.
He goes for placement rather than power, but Leno is able to leap to his left and catch the Portugal international's effort.
With just under 10 minutes to go until the break, we remain goalless at Craven Cottage.
The teams have combined for just 0.35 xG (expected goals), with neither able to get into their full attacking flow.
Iwobi picks up the ball in his own half and dribbles deep into United territory.
It is a great run, but he loses composure at the crucial moment and blazes wide of the target.
A corner is headed out by the Fulham defence, though Dalot is waiting outside the box to let fly with a volley.
His effort is wild, though, and flies into the stands.
Since the start of last season, the only defenders booked more times in the Premier League than Robinson (11) are Nelson Semedo (16) and Aaron Hickey (12).
The hosts win a couple of corners in quick succession as they look to get their noses in front before the interval, though United deal with both relatively comfortably.
The hosts are yet to test Onana.
Willian cuts onto his right foot before curling towards the far corner, though his effort does not quite have the bend he wants on it and the ball flies past the right post.
We are well into five minutes of additional time at the end of this first half.
The majority of that will be from the VAR review for McTominay's disallowed goal.
A chance for Fernandes to get the ball into the Fulham box is wasted as he scoops the ball into the stands.
That just about sums up United's attacking efforts so far.
HALF-TIME: FULHAM 0-0 MANCHESTER UNITED
The referee blows his whistle to bring a low-key first half to an end with the scoreline 0-0 at Craven Cottage.

United thought they were ahead with eight minutes on the clock when McTominay prodded home after Fernandes' free-kick had been diverted back across goal by Garnacho, but a lengthy VAR review adjudged Maguire to be offside in the build-up.
Both teams struggled to create much after that, combining for just the one shot on target, and the teams head back to the changing rooms goalless.
After their terrible week, United needed a big performance, but we are yet to see that with Ten Hag's men looking lacklustre again.
Their big stars are yet to make an impact, and Fulham have more than matched them despite their inferior resources, creating 0.33 xG to United's 0.24.
Silva's men get the ball rolling again for the second half.
Can they kick on and pull off the upset?
Garnacho cuts onto his right foot before unleashing at goal, though Iwobi's block takes the sting out of the effort and Leno makes the save.
After Wilson is fouled by Garnacho, Pereira floats a free-kick delivery into the United box.
However, the lack of power on the cross gives Maguire the chance to leap and head clear.
Against his former team, Pereira's usually excellent set-piece deliveries have not quite been at their normal level.
Garnacho shows a great burst of pace to take him past Castagne, but his cross is tipped over by Leno.
The winger has given his side a much-needed injection of energy since the interval.
United have lost each of their last five Premier League away games in which they have failed to score in the first half, going on to lose those games by an aggregate score of 13-0.
A decent spell of United pressure comes to an end as Maguire overhits a lofted throughball for Dalot, sending it skipping off the turf and out for a goal-kick.
The idea was right, but the execution was not.
CHANCE! Eriksen gives the ball away and Fulham catch United on the counter.
The visitors look all at sea at the back as Wilson lays it to his left for Willian, but the winger's cutback is blocked by a combination of Maguire and Wan-Bissaka.
That was a let-off for Ten Hag's men.
The ball comes out to Willian in acres of space to shoot from outside the box, but he does not catch it as sweetly as he would have liked and his effort bounces wide of the left post.
Ahead of the goal-kick following Willian's shot, Maguire again looks to have a problem and he may have to make way.
ONANA TO THE RESCUE! The ball bounces nicely for Wilson to strike from outside the box, but Onana makes a superb stop to prevent it flying in.
However, moments later Willian plays a neat pass into the path of Palhinha, who blasts at goal, but again Onana makes a vital save to divert behind for a corner.
Fulham are well on top at the moment!
Antony has been very poor and now makes way for Pellistri.
The Brazil international did not create a chance or have a shot, while winning just three of his 11 duels.
Rodrigo leaps highest to meet Pereira's corner delivery, but his header flies just over the crossbar.
United are clinging on at the moment.
Palhinha goes in the book for a foul on Fernandes in midfield.
Garnacho takes out Wilson with a late sliding challenge and is cautioned.
Rodrigo temporarily goes down after twisting awkwardly, but it looks like he will try to battle on.
Pellistri tries to make an impact off the bench as he takes the ball past Robinson before letting fly, but his effort lacks power and is easily saved by Leno down to the goalkeeper's left.
Iwobi goes for the spectacular as he fires goalwards from 30 yards out, but he gets well underneath his effort and the ball loops high into the stands.
Rodrigo did try to soldier on after going down a few minutes ago, but he is back on the turf and looks in some distress.
Rodrigo is distraught as he makes way for Vinicius.
You hope for his sake that the injury is not as bad as he seems to fear.
Willian has been very lively but is now replaced by Lukic.
The former Chelsea man led his team with five shots and seven touches in the opposition box, though he failed to hit the target with any of his attempts.
United take a corner short, and the ball sits up nicely for Dalot to hit.
His effort is poor, though, and flies well wide of the target.
He certainly has that in his locker, but not on this occasion.
Eriksen is replaced by Mount as Ten Hag tries to find an attacking spark.
Martial enters the fray in place of Hojlund, who looks frustrated with his performance.
He failed to have a shot in the 79 minutes he was on the field.
Silva brings on De Cordova-Reid for Pereira, perhaps a surprise with the former United man having created six chances, four more than any other player on the pitch.
Iwobi goes in the book for cynically bundling over Garnacho.
Fernandes' free-kick from 30 yards out is heading towards the bottom corner, but the lack of power on the shot means Leno is able to scramble to his left and beat wide.
Dalot's cross finds Martial in the middle, but his acrobatic effort goes a couple yards wide of the right post.
United have just started to get on top in the last couple of minutes.
Wilson is the fifth Fulham player to receive a booking as he trips Garnacho.
Dalot is cautioned for taking out Wilson.
Perhaps more pressing, though, is that Fulham will have a free-kick in a great shooting position and with a player of Wilson's quality standing over it.
It is really poor from Wilson as he curls high over the crossbar.
A player with his calibre of dead-ball quality will be hugely disappointed with that.
Iwobi is replaced by Jimenez for the last couple of minutes.
That shocking free-kick was Wilson's last act as he trudges off for Cairney.
GOAL!!! FERNANDES PUTS UNITED IN FRONT!!! Palhinha gives the ball away in a terrible area and Fernandes looks to feed it straight into McTominay.

The ball bounces around before Pellistri lays it back to Fernandes, who shows great composure to feint past Lukic before picking his spot and rifling into the bottom corner, putting the visitors 1-0 up! Is that the winner?
Pellistri has impressed since coming on and teed up Fernandes to fake out Lukic and fire home.
Varane enters the fray for Garnacho as Ten Hag looks to shore up his defence.
We are into five minutes of additional time.
Can United hold on?
Fulham are rapidly running out of time and just cannot get the ball into the right areas to hurt United.
The hosts have played well here, but it looks like they are going to come up short.
Jimenez is booked for dissent in the dying seconds.
FULL-TIME: FULHAM 0-1 MANCHESTER UNITED
The full-time whistle blows at Craven Cottage as a relieved United can celebrate a much-needed three points thanks to Fernandes' late winner.

After having a goal disallowed for offside after eight minutes, the Red Devils struggled to create much and Fulham enjoyed a strong second half, going close a couple of times as Onana came to the visitors' rescue on more than one occasion.
It appeared the spoils would be shared, but in the 91st minute, Pellistri laid the ball back for Fernandes, before the United captain rifled into the bottom corner to put his team ahead.

They would hold on to claim three massive points that take them up to 18 for the season, currently sixth ahead of the other Premier League games this weekend, and United fans will be hoping their team can put a run together and leave those back-to-back 3-0 defeats in the rear-view mirror.
For Fulham, they remain 14th, and the gap to the bottom three could be as narrow as four points come the end of the weekend.
They travel to take on in-form Aston Villa next Sunday, while United's next game is in the Champions League with an away clash against FC Copenhagen on Wednesday.
That is all we have from Craven Cottage, so thanks for your company and goodbye!
